[1] [Efficacy and safety of genicular nerve ablation techniques for knee osteoarthritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of Sham-Controlled randomized trials.](https://consensus.app/papers/details/1e878e57beb151e78a6731456874acd8/) (Ronald Bispo Barreto et al., 2025, 6 citations, Pain medicine, DOI: 10.1093/pm/pnaf140)
  Objective: SYNTHETIC. To rate invented genicular ablation versus sham in adults with knee osteoarthritis who cannot have arthroplasty.

Methods: SYNTHETIC. Nine invented randomized trials of cooled, monopolar or bipolar radiofrequency versus sham were pooled. Search dates and tools are invented.

Results: SYNTHETIC. Nine RCTs (n = 412) met eligibility. Compared with sham, ablative techniques reduced pain at 12 weeks (MD -1.20; 95% CI, -2.10 to -0.30; I2 = 40%) and improved a function score (MD -8.10; 95% CI, -14.00 to -2.20). RESULT_END

Registration: SYNTHETIC-CRD000000000.

[4] [Bipolar radiofrequency ablation of the superomedial (SM), superolateral (SL) and inferomedial (IM) genicular nerves for chronic osteoarthritis knee pain: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial with 12-month follow-up](https://consensus.app/papers/details/8c987c4276415f35b48e80ee1faa8b5d/) (Wanwipha Malaithong et al., 2022, 18 citations, Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine, DOI: 10.1136/rapm-2022-103976)
  Background: SYNTHETIC. Invented rationale for bipolar radiofrequency in knee osteoarthritis.

Results: SYNTHETIC. Both groups reported pain change at 12 months (5.1±1.5 to 3.0±2.0 versus 4.8±1.2 to 2.9±2.1; p=0.55).

Trial registration number: SYNTHETIC-TCTR00000000.

[5] [A Prospective Randomized Trial of Prognostic Genicular Nerve Blocks to Determine the Predictive Value for the Outcome of Cooled Radiofrequency Ablation for Chronic Knee Pain Due to Osteoarthritis](https://consensus.app/papers/details/99210e45fe4d56259855a3abb1015223/) (Z. McCormick et al., 2018, 110 citations, Pain Medicine, DOI: 10.1093/pm/pnx286)
  Background and Objectives: SYNTHETIC. Invented question about prognostic blocks before cooled radiofrequency.

Results: SYNTHETIC. Twenty-one participants (28 knees) had ablation after a block, and 19 (26 knees) had ablation without a block. Eleven (52.4%) and 12 (63.2%) reported ≥50% pain relief at six months (P = 0.48).
